delivered.statement: Order inflows grew from Rs 1.7T FY21 to Rs 4.4T FY26, 20% CAGR vs 14% guidance
Revenue grew from Rs 1.4T to Rs 2.9T, delivering 16% CAGR against 15% planned
ROE improved from ~10% at plan start to 16.6% in FY26 (excluding Labour Code provision impact)
Order book stands at Rs 7.40 trillion as of March 2026, a 28% YoY increase
Group revenues grew 11% YoY to Rs 828B in Q4 FY26 despite West Asia impact
Net Working Capital to Revenue ratio improved sharply to 4.1%, 690 basis points YoY improvement
Energy segment total order inflow crossed Rs 1 trillion for first time in FY26
Recurring PAT for Q4 FY26 at Rs 53 billion, up 5% on year-on-year basis
Realty business doubled its pre-sales to Rs 94 billion in FY26
Commissioned 12 MW at Kanchipuram, additional 6 MW at advanced commissioning stage, total 30 MW
MSCI ESG rating upgraded from BBB to A in November 2025

themes: Middle East resilience and growth: Rs 3T order book, USD 55B capex announced by UAE, re-tendering expected across GCC
Margin stability amid transition: PPM at 7.8%, legacy Energy projects closing, new order execution ramp-up ahead
New growth engines scaling: Rs 50B+ capex into Electronics, Semiconductors, Green Hydrogen, Data Centers over five years
Modular manufacturing expansion: Reducing site intensity via fabrication, enabling geographic diversity and global market access
Supply chain cost management: Logistics and insurance costs elevated; active client negotiations for relief and cost-sharing
Realty restructuring and scaling: Consolidated entity, 100M sqft portfolio target, 25% pre-sales CAGR planned
risks: West Asia geopolitical disruption impacting execution timelines, logistics inflation, and project progress extending into H1 FY27
Fixed-price Energy contracts exposed to commodity and logistics cost inflation; customer compensation mechanism uncertain
Legacy Hydrocarbon project margin drag persisting; closure completed but defects liability period extends through FY27
Working capital deterioration risk: Ratio normalizing from 4.1% to 10% as customer advances consumed progressively in FY27

analyst_pushback.question: Why did Q4 revenue miss FY26 guidance despite Q3 confidence?
analyst_pushback.response: Lost roughly Rs 50 billion in Q4 from supply chain issues impacting Infrastructure, Power Transmission, Renewables segments

analyst_pushback.question: What contractual protections exist for fixed-price Middle East contracts amid cost inflation?
analyst_pushback.response: Infrastructure projects have price adjustment provisions. Energy contracts fixed lump-sum but customers open to negotiations on cost relief

analyst_pushback.question: Won't new ultra-mega orders at early stage weigh on Energy margins further?
analyst_pushback.response: Legacy projects completed, no further cost creeps expected. Newer project execution should improve Energy segment margins going forward

analyst_pushback.question: Why did prospects pipeline decline 6% despite strong bidding activity?
analyst_pushback.response: Pipeline timing reflects phasing of large bids. Capex outlook positive; re-tendering expected this year, Middle East a core growth market

tone_evidence: Confident on Middle East prospects and order pipelines; cautious on FY27 execution due to West Asia conflict disruptions
